points.description: States that linked lists are dynamic (can grow/shrink at run time), so they can hold a variable number of elements, unlike fixed-size arrays.
points.partial_credit: Half or more if only vaguely stated (e.g. 'flexible' or 'easy to add/remove elements' without size/dynamic idea).

points.description: Uses the term 'dynamic' (or equivalent: size changes at run time / no fixed size) to describe the linked list.

rubric.notes: Full marks for saying linked lists are dynamic / can change size, storing a variable number of elements, in any wording, even briefly. Part marks for vague statements such as easy insertion/deletion or flexibility without the size idea. No marks for unrelated points (e.g. only memory addresses, speed of access) or for claiming arrays are better.
